text:
maya: Heads-up — brought up the per-layer dynamic-quant (dynq-v2) build on the reranker smokebench and seeing an odd signal: ndcg@10 is slightly up but mrr@1 drops on short queries (~<10 tokens). Anyone else hit this pattern?

samir: hmm. numbers? short queries meaning top-k candidates count?

maya: quick summary from local eval harness:
```
model: rerank-dynq-v2
dataset: rerank-holdout-v3 (stratified)
seed: 42
metrics: ndcg@10 +0.6% (overall), mrr@1 -1.8% (short queries slice)
candidates: top50 from retrieval
config: per-layer scale + asymmetric clipping, batch_size=64
```

maya: full logs attached in cloud run but pasted top diff — ndcg uptick driven by mid-tail, top1 accuracy falls on short queries only. :thinking_face:

jin: could be candidate scoring reshuffle — quantization changes tiny relative scores so ties break differently, hurting top1 while ranking otherwise ok. did you check score distribution shift?

maya: yes, score histogram shows tighter cluster for top10 on short queries (stdev down ~12%). seems like less separation.

rachel: two quick asks: 1) run the same eval with deterministic tie-breaker (seeded stable-sort) to see if it's tie noise; 2) test with candidate pruning to top20 to see sensitivity.

maya: on it. running seeded stable-sort and top20 prune now. command I used:
```bash
./tools/eval_rerank --model rerank-dynq-v2 --holdout rerank-holdout-v3 --seed 42 --topk 50 --metrics ndcg, mrr --slice short_query
```

evalbot: job 3311223344-1 queued, will post results. ETA ~6m. :gear:

samir: also check tokenizer/priming differences — dynq build used newer tokenizer mapping that collapses some punctuation; short queries are sensitive to punctuation anchors. try old-tokenizer run too.

maya: good call — that slipped past me. will re-run with tok_v1.

jin: one more thought — per-layer scale tends to compress logits for early layers. try asym scaling variant where head layers keep fp16 range (config flag: --preserve-heads). might recover top1.

rachel: if this is real, we should plan an A/B that stratifies by query len buckets and measures both ndcg@10 and mrr@1. don't let overall ndcg drive rollout if top1 user impact is negative.

maya: agreed. triage plan:
- reproduce with stable-sort + top20 + tok_v1
- try --preserve-heads variant
- run stratified A/B plan doc (I'll draft)

maya: posting preliminary seeded stable-sort log:
```
short_slice: mrr@1 -1.81% (seeded stable-sort)
short_slice_top20: mrr@1 -1.12%
overall_ndcg@10 +0.55%
```

samir: ok shrink but still there. top20 helps — indicates tail noise dilution. could be retrieval pool interaction.

evalbot: job 3311223344-2 (tok_v1 + preserve-heads) completed: short_slice mrr@1 -0.25%, overall ndcg@10 +0.4%

maya: awesome — preserve-heads looks promising. running a quick canary A/B with small traffic in staging dedicated to confirm before any prod rollout.

rachel: please capture per-query examples where ordering flipped. need to inspect user-visible change. add human-readable snippets to the A/B review doc.

maya: will do. thanks all. :thumbsup:

jin: nice debugging loop, great to see small config knob recover top1. keep me posted if canary shows any regression in other slices.

maya: will update thread with canary outcome and attach example diffs.

(ended)
